purpose: Explain why the two single-gate reserve candidates fail before choosing any global fix.

targets.why_detail: The score failure is attributable to the evidence selected in the frozen candidate state: a broad platform-strategy/ thought-leadership article, not a concrete catalog/product-data pain signal. The existing candidate note already says the evidence is broad and not specific enough. A stronger September 2026 KEF Shopify Plus migration case now exists, so the next action should be source substitution/re-evaluation under the same rubric rather than changing the global scoring rubric first.

stronger_evidence_found.notes: Concrete Shopify Plus migration, integration and multi-market implementation case authored by Paul Sanderson.

targets.fix_implication: Do not widen/loosen the global scoring rubric based on CTG alone. First test whether replacing the weak source with the stronger dated case changes the score under the existing Run-C rubric.

targets.why_detail: Current management is public, but the fixed PIM/MDM matrix only accepts CTO / Head of Delivery / Solution(s) Architect / Managing Partner. 7thSENSE publicly lists two CEOs plus Head of Project Management, Head of Consulting & Sales, Head of Software Development and Head of IT. The candidate was excluded because none of those exact titles match the matrix, not because no management exists.
targets.fix_implication: If changing the role matrix, test a principled matrix extension (for example CEO and/or project/delivery-equivalent leadership) across all 12 candidates. Do not add a 7thSENSE-specific override.

decision_note: The why-diagnostic weakens a generic score-first plan: CTG's failure points to weak selected evidence, whereas 7thSENSE points to role-matrix coverage. Any next experiment should target the diagnosed cause, not merely the visible gate.
